title: Features
summary: Diceroll's Settings → Features: the six features as one list in canonical order, each row with its switch, its facts as status and its own settings nested under it. Sign-in is off, so Cloud Sync can't be turned on and says why; Commerce is on because Licensing is; raw service slugs and the derived registration are folded, read-only, in one 'Slugs and device registration' row.
compare: Features is the first tab of the product Settings hub (Features, Presentation, Keys & secrets, Members); Settings is active in the sidebar foot and the crumbs read Diceroll › Settings.

Exactly six rows in canonical order: Licensing, Managed config, Ship builds, Sign-in, Cloud Sync, Commerce. Each has its service glyph tile, its name, a Status column and one switch, with no description under the name (owner, 2026-10-09). No raw slugs (license, distribution, update) appear outside the 'Slugs and device registration' row.

The requirement rule is stated once, in a callout above the list (in the 400px aside at wide): a feature turns on only when what it needs is on; turning one off turns off what needs it too, in one change you confirm.

Requirements read both ways on the rows (kit .reqs): Licensing says 'Needed by Commerce', Managed config and Sign-in 'Needed by Cloud Sync', with a link mark. On the dependents each requirement has its own mark, never colour alone, and an accessible name with its state: Commerce 'Needs ✓ Licensing'; Cloud Sync 'Needs ✓ Managed config 🔒 Sign-in'.

Cloud Sync's switch is disabled (not merely off) while Sign-in is off, and its status 'Turn on Sign-in first' is a link that moves focus to Sign-in's switch. Turning on Sign-in enables Cloud Sync but never turns it on by itself.

A feature's own switches sit in a sunken box under its text (kit .feature-subs): Managed config → Minted tokens ('Diceroll declares multiplayer.roomToken.'); Ship builds → In-app updates (one fact per line: 'The Godot updater', then 'Store builds update through their store'), Packages ('On pkg.plrs.im'; off; glossary: Packages, not Package feeds) and Polaris Key storefront (Unlisted / Eligible / Everyone, one setting, two lines: 'Who finds Diceroll on key.plrs.im', then 'Eligible: owns it or qualifies'); Sign-in → Customer portal, its name only.
An off feature's own switches stay visible but disabled with 'Turns on with Sign-in'; an off feature's tile is muted and its status cell stays empty, because its switch already says Off.

Status column (headed 'Status' over the rows, kit .feature-rows-head) shows facts as status text, never pills: 'Verified on 4 platforms' over '3 tiers · 18,406 licenses', 'Catalog v6 published', '1.8.2 on stable' over its channels, '3 storefronts ready' over 'itch.io isn't set up yet'.
Turning on Ship builds writes release, distribution and update in one audited change; the page never shows them as three switches.

Every turn-off confirms before anything changes (ADMIN.md §5.2: disabling a service is L1): a caution dialog listing what stops when nothing else turns off; a danger dialog naming each dependent when they turn off too, as products.turn-off-licensing does for Licensing.
'Slugs and device registration' is one folded row (its name says what it holds, so it has no sub-line), read-only, with Show.

Phone: the column header hides, each row puts the switch top-right beside the name, status drops under the name, nested switches span the full width, the Discover segmented control sits under its text, every switch is 44×24, and the tab strip fades at its right edge where it scrolls.
Every switch is the console accent: one track colour and one knob colour in both themes. The service colour stays on each row's glyph tile.
A switch that turns something on applies at once: it shows a spinner while saving; a failed save puts the switch back and shows an inline error on the row saying what went wrong and how to retry.
The Diceroll sidebar shows one count, on Devices (26,315, ST-36's device pill).

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Masthead mark (B4): from 1024px a 48px flat tile on this page (the feature's glyph on a landing page, the product's icon on a product page) replaces the orientation chip; below 1024 the chip carries the context; never on a dense data page, a record or a state page.
The features table spans the canvas (no 1200px cap); prose in it stays at 72ch; the hub's four tabs are an underline tablist; History is a ghost (admin-1-36).
Feature rows keep a subtle glyph tile, never a solid accent chip, and no accent top-rule cards (site-08 dropped: accent marks context only, B2/B6).

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: every switch is the console's colour with one knob colour, requirements carry their own marks, and the missing save and confirm states are specified.

findings.issue: Every switch took its feature's service accent (lime, gold, cyan, green), and in light the knob flipped between near-black and white from row to row.
findings.resolution: data-service moved from each row to its icon tile, so every switch inherits the console accent and its knob colour in both themes.

findings.issue: 'Package feeds' against glossary §2's 'Packages'; Ship builds lists itch.io as a channel while Commerce said 'itch.io needs its channel first'; the storefront help was hard to parse; 'On by default' beside an on switch read as a state.
findings.resolution: Switch renamed 'Packages' (glossary §2 already says so; lead: ST-38's scope text still says 'Package feeds' and should follow). Commerce reads 'itch.io's storefront isn't set up yet.' Storefront help rewritten as suggested. 'On by default when Ship builds turns on.' moved into In-app updates' description.

findings.issue: Cloud Sync showed a met requirement only by colour under one lock; Commerce's met state was a barely different open lock.
findings.resolution: Each requirement has its own mark: '✓ Managed config is on', '🔒 Sign-in is off', '✓ Licensing is on'. 'Turn on Sign-in first' is a link to Sign-in's row.

findings.issue: No pending or failed look for an immediate-apply switch; the compare only promised a confirmation with dependents; on phone the tabs cut 'Membe…' with no cue and switches were 36×20.
findings.resolution: Compare now says every turn-off confirms (caution without dependents, danger with them), a switch shows a spinner while saving, and a failed save reverts it with an inline row error. On phone the tab strip fades at the right edge and switches are 44×24.

findings.issue: The 'A feature turns on only when…' callout floated alone over a 1000px void beside an empty wide rail.
findings.resolution: Callout and wide rail are deleted. The table fills a content column capped at about 1200px, left-aligned with the page title, with a fixed 280px single-line Status column so name, status and toggle sit close together. The Needs lines and the confirm dialog teach the rule.

findings.issue: Dependencies were told three ways (Needed by, Needs, a purple 'Turn on Sign-in first').
findings.resolution: One dependency fact and one status fact per row: 'Needs …' stays on the dependent, 'Needed by …' is gone from the providers, the purple cell is gone from Cloud Sync, 'Turns on with Sign-in' is gone from Customer portal. Status is one line (3 tiers · 18,406 licenses; Catalog v6 published; 1.8.2 on stable; 3 of 4 storefronts ready) with a muted 'Off' in the empty cells; 'Verified on 4 platforms' is dropped (Integration owns it).

findings.issue: Nested groups came in two styles and Advanced was a third card style; sub-copy was long.
findings.resolution: One inset panel (8px radius, 16px padding, 1px dividers) reaching 17px past the text column so a sub-row's title lines up with the parent's and its control with the parent's switch; Advanced is a last row of the same table. Storefront, In-app updates, Customer portal and Advanced use the lead's copy.

findings.issue: Disabled text under 3:1; each phone row about 170px tall with status far from its toggle; 'Members' cropped.
findings.resolution: Disabled and locked rows dim only the control: text stays 4.5:1 and an off track keeps a 3:1 edge. On phone the status is one line under the title and the description hides below 480px. The tab strip has 12px between tabs and a right fade, so all four tabs show at 390.

findings.issue: Draw extra states: saving, failed save, permission-denied, Advanced open.
findings.resolution: declined: Outside this spacing pass, which keeps existing content and states; backlog.

findings.issue: Fill the wide aside with History, an Advanced summary or a '5 of 6 on' summary.
findings.resolution: declined: It adds content and duplicates History and Overview; the rail is removed instead.

findings.issue: Cap the table at 960px and centre it, or put the toggle next to the title.
findings.resolution: declined: Centring breaks the shared left alignment with the title and tabs; the 1200px cap with a 280px status column closes the gap without it, and a toggle beside the title breaks the kit's switch-column pattern.

findings.issue: Delete the 'Needed by' lines and keep a 7-word hint under the title.
findings.resolution: declined: No hint is kept: the callout is deleted outright and 'Needed by' is dropped with the dependent's Needs as the single direction.
